subject: Coord: AWS private offer — buyer consent windows & term sync
messages:
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.k@redwood.com>
To: Aisha Patel <aisha.p@healthgrid.com>, Tom Walker <tom.walker@cloudbuy.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.o@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.i@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 18 Aug 2026 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Coord: AWS private offer — buyer consent windows & term sync

Aisha / Tom —

Thanks again for the call this morning. To keep the AWS private-offer flow moving I want to align on two gating pieces we need from HealthGrid procurement and for Redwood to commit on:

1) Buyer approval window (how long they need to review the PO/private offer once we submit).
2) Term length options you want surfaced in the private offer (12m / 24m / 36m?) and whether one needs explicit legal sign-off.

I attached a short approval matrix with our suggested defaults for co-sell credits and procurement windows. High level proposal:
- Submit private offer with two term options: 12-month (standard) + 24-month (discounted).
- Buyer approval window: 7 business days by default; escalate path to buyer legal if beyond 10 business days.
- Co-sell entitlements: assign Redwood AM / AWS co-sell lead once PO accepted; will require buyer consent checkbox in DocuSign.

Can you confirm HealthGrid's internal review SLA and whether Tom needs us to route legal concurrently? If there are any constraints from AWS Marketplace on multi-term private offers I can loop Karthik/Vanessa to reconcile.

Next steps I suggest:
- Aisha to confirm approval SLA (reply by EOD Thu).
- Redwood to prepare two-line private-offer payload + proposal PDF for signature.
- Vanessa to prepare internal marketplace routing + co-sell resource assignment guidance.

Thanks —
Vivek Kulkarni
Director, Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference
M: +1 (650) 555-0142

Attachment: HealthGrid_MAL_approval_matrix.xlsx (spreadsheet stub)

From: Aisha Patel <aisha.p@healthgrid.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.k@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Walker <tom.walker@cloudbuy.com>
Date: Tue, 18 Aug 2026 11:03:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Coord: AWS private offer — buyer consent windows & term sync

Vivek —

Thanks for the summary and the matrix. Quick answers from our side:

- Approval SLA: Our procurement generally asks for 5 business days for a standard private-offer review. For larger (> $150k ARR) or any amendments we typically require 10 business days plus legal review.
- Term lengths: We prefer a 12-month term as default; 24-months is OK if pricing delta is >12% and exec approves. 36-months would need CFO sign-off and internal forecasting alignment.
- Routing: Please route the private offer to procurement@healthgrid.com and cc legal@healthgrid.com. Tom is our procurement lead and will coordinate timing.

One ask: can Redwood include a checkbox in the signature flow that grants AWS/Redwood permission for co-sell introductions? Our legal wants explicit buyer consent documented.

Tom — are you OK with the proposed 5/10 business day windows?

Best,
Aisha Patel
SVP, Product & Partnerships
HealthGrid

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.c@redwood.com>, Aisha Patel <aisha.p@healthgrid.com>
Date: Wed, 19 Aug 2026 08:46:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Coord: AWS private offer — buyer consent windows & term sync

Vivek / team —

Thanks — quick internal notes after checking Marketplace guidance and co-sell ops:

1) AWS Marketplace private offer can include multiple SKUs/term options, but pricing tiers need to be explicit. We should surface 12m and 24m as separate SKUs in the offer to avoid ambiguity during procurement.
2) Buyer approval window: marketplace metadata doesn't enforce a hard SLA; it's on the buyer side. We recommend shipping the private-offer and setting the internal expectation to 7 business days for Procurement review, but include a 10-business-day auto-escalation to account for legal review. (Matches Aisha's ask.)
3) Consent for co-sell intros: include a consent checkbox and record the signed timestamp in the DocuSign payload saved to the Drive link in related_links. Legal prefers the language: "I consent to introductions by Redwood and AWS for co-selling and joint GTM activities."
4) Co-sell crediting: To simplify, we recommend Redwood request AWS co-sell credit at standard rate for the first year; any additional crediting requirements for a 24m renewal will be handled post-acceptance and recorded in a co-sell MOU.

Action items assigned:
- Vanessa: build the two SKUs in the offer, attach the PROPOSAL_Redwood-HealthGrid-v1.pdf, and create the DocuSign template with consent checkbox. (ETA: EOD Thu 8/20)
- Karthik: sanity-check pricing and discount table versus our internal discount tiers (ETA: EOD Wed)
- Vivek: confirm buyer approval window and routing once Aisha confirms.

I will also coordinate with Marketplace ops to ensure the private offer fields map cleanly to AWS's approval flow (avoids back-and-forth).

Vanessa Ortiz
Sr. Marketplace Programs | Redwood Inference

Aisha / Tom —

Appreciate the fast responses. We will proceed as follows:

1) Redwood will build the private offer with two explicit SKUs: 12-month (base) and 24-month (discounted). Pricing table and PROPOSAL_Redwood-HealthGrid-v1.pdf attached.
2) We will route to procurement@healthgrid.com and cc legal@healthgrid.com when we submit the private offer.
3) Buyer approval window per your preference: set expectation at 5 business days for standard review; mark 10 business days for formal legal escalation.
4) DocuSign template will include the consent checkbox language Vanessa suggested — we will capture the signed timestamp and store the envelope PDF in the Drive link.

Vanessa will post the offer & DocuSign by EOD today. Karthik and Marissa are copied to prepare internal approval and finance checks.

Next meeting: propose a quick 15-min handoff tomorrow at 10am PT (optional) to walk the procurement owner through the DocuSign flow. Please confirm availability.

Thanks —
Vivek
Director, Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference
